Draw a blinded sample for human coding

coding_sample.Rd

Draws a sheet of documents and questions with a blank column for a coder, and the model's answer withheld, and writes it as a CSV when file is given. A coder shown the model's label agrees with it more often, so withholding it is what makes the resulting agreement figure interpretable.

Usage

coding_sample(
  results,
  docs = NULL,
  ...,
  text = NULL,
  id = NULL,
  image = NULL,
  n = 200L,
  items = NULL,
  labels_allowed = NULL,
  copy_media = TRUE,
  file = NULL,
  seed = 1234L
)

Arguments

results

A fathom_results object from measure() or read_checkpoints().

docs

A character vector, or the data frame passed to measure(). Default is NULL, which uses the documents a character-vector run stored on the results.

...

Not used, and refused if anything reaches it. Every argument after it is name-only, so a misspelling lands here rather than being matched by position.

text, id

Strings naming the text and identifier columns, if docs is a data frame. text is then required, and id defaults to the row position.

image

A string naming a column in docs holding the media for each document, so the sheet carries it as well as any text. A character column is one file per document. A list column holds several, such as the frames prepare_video() returns, and they share one cell joined with |. Default is NULL.

n

An integer giving the total document-item pairs to draw, across all questions. Default is 200.

items

A character vector restricting the draw to specific items, or NULL (the default) for all of them.

labels_allowed

A character vector of permitted values for the human_label column, written into the sheet so a coder knows the answer scheme. Defaults to the instrument label names.

copy_media

A logical value indicating whether to copy the files image points at into a folder beside the CSV and rewrite the column relative to it. Acts only when both file and image are given. FALSE leaves the original absolute paths, which is right when the coders share the filesystem the sheet was written on and wrong otherwise. Default is TRUE.

file

A string giving the path to write the CSV to, or NULL (the default) to write nothing.

seed

An integer giving the seed for the draw, so the same call draws the same rows. The session's random stream is put back afterwards, so this seed reaches the draw and nothing after it. NULL draws from the session's stream instead. Default is 1234.

Value

A tibble with one row per document-item pair drawn, in random order so the order leaks nothing about the draw. The same document appears once per item it was drawn on.

The columns are for the coder, the document last so the others stay on screen beside it.

  • id is the document identifier, matching the results.

  • item names which question this row is about.

  • question is the question text as the model received it, so a coder answers the same question rather than a paraphrase of it. NA when the results carry no instrument.

  • allowed holds the permitted answers, pipe-separated, so the sheet states its own answer scheme.

  • human_label is blank, for the coder to fill with one value from allowed. The model's answer is deliberately absent.

  • note is blank, for the coder. Nothing reads it, and it exists so a coder has somewhere to record a case they were unsure about.

  • text is the document, in full.

  • image is the file image named, or NA when none was. Several files, a video window's frames, are joined in order with |, the way allowed joins the answers. Rewritten relative to the CSV when copy_media acted.

The draw

Every document-item pair has the same chance of being drawn, and the budget is split across questions in proportion to how many pairs each one has, so a figure computed on the sheet is already a figure about the corpus.

Item is a stratification variable rather than a filter, so the draw runs within each question and n stays the total across them. The draw is systematic, so the sample is exactly n rows on every call. An n at or above the number of pairs is a census.

See also

validate_sample(), which reads the coded sheet, and coder_reference() for collapsing several coders into one.

Examples

# Results from a real run ship with the package, so this needs no server.
p <- system.file("extdata", "vignette_results.rds", package = "fathom")
baked <- readRDS(p)
sheet <- coding_sample(baked$res_six, parlasent, text = "sentence",
  id = "id", n = 20, seed = 1234)
#> Blinded coding sample
#> 
#> Pairs         20 across 1 item
#> Drawn         20 of 100
#> 
#> Tip      Pass the completed sheet to validate_sample() together with these
#>          results.
head(sheet)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 8
#>   id     item     question                 allowed human_label note  text  image
#>   <chr>  <chr>    <chr>                    <chr>   <chr>       <chr> <chr> <chr>

#> 2 uk_049 category "Where does this senten… 1 | 2 … NA          NA    Pres… NA   
#> 3 uk_032 category "Where does this senten… 1 | 2 … NA          NA    Does… NA   
#> 4 uk_073 category "Where does this senten… 1 | 2 … NA          NA    For … NA   
#> 5 uk_047 category "Where does this senten… 1 | 2 … NA          NA    The … NA   
#> 6 uk_036 category "Where does this senten… 1 | 2 … NA          NA    So w… NA
